title: How to Tell if Points Are Collinear

scenes.title: Do these points lie on one straight line?
body: Collinear means all the points share one straight line.
scenes.narration: Suppose you are given the points negative one negative one, zero one, and one three. The question is not whether they look roughly lined up. Collinear means they lie on exactly one straight line. The clean test is to check whether the direction from one point to the next stays the same.

scenes.title: Direction is measured by slope
body: Slope = change in y divided by change in x.
For A to B: rise 2, run 1.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea: slope measures direction. From A to B, y rises by two while x moves right by one, so the slope is two. Students often lose a negative sign here. One minus negative one is two, and zero minus negative one is one.

scenes.title: Compare the next segment the same way
body: For B to C: rise 2, run 1.
Use the same subtraction order in top and bottom.
scenes.narration: Now compare B to C. The change in y is three minus one, which is two, and the change in x is one minus zero, which is one. The slope is two again. A common mistake is reversing only one subtraction. If you reverse the y subtraction, reverse the x subtraction too, or the sign will be wrong.

scenes.title: Why equal slopes prove one line
scenes.narration: Both slopes are two, so the direction from A to B is exactly the same as the direction from B to C. That means the path never bends or changes direction. All three points lie on the same line, y equals two x plus one.

scenes.title: Quick check: are they collinear?
body: Vertical exception: all x-values must be equal.
scenes.narration: So yes, these points are collinear. The key idea is not memorizing a test; it is checking whether the direction stays constant. For nonvertical points, compare slopes. If the line is vertical, slope is undefined, so instead check that every x coordinate is the same. The full lesson is available on SUMMIT. Find the complete lesson below.
